podcast.title: Newest Member (1972) - American Guitarist
podcast.body: Bob Welch joined Fleetwood Mac as their newest member around 1972, bringing his American guitar style to the band. He contributed significantly to albums like *Bare Trees*, *Penguin*, and *Mystery to Me*, often taking on primary songwriting duties with Christine McVie. "Plus the contributions of Fleetwood Mac's newest member, American guitarist Bob Welch."

podcast.title: Departure from Fleetwood Mac - End of 1974
podcast.body: Bob Welch left Fleetwood Mac at the end of 1974, after the release of the *Heroes Are Hard to Find* album, reportedly due to his own personal and professional issues. His departure created the vacancy that Mick Fleetwood filled by recruiting Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks. "Meanwhile Heroes Are Hard to Find turned out to be the last album for Bob Welch, who was dealing with his own personal and professional issues. He left the group at the end of 1974."

podcast.title: Departure from Fleetwood Mac (Pre-1975)
podcast.body: His departure from Fleetwood Mac created a vacancy that was subsequently filled by Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks in 1975, marking a significant shift in the band's lineup. "The void. That was left when Bob Welch left the band so you have a pair of American folk rock singer songwriters Buckingham and Nicks joining the drummer Mick Fleetwood the bassist John McVee and keyboard player and singer songwriter Christine McVee yes John's wife."

podcast.title: Primary Songwriting Duties - Post Kirwan Departure
podcast.body: After Danny Kirwan was fired in 1972, Bob Welch and Christine McVie assumed primary songwriting duties for Fleetwood Mac. They sought to expand the band's sound even further on subsequent albums like *Penguin* and *Mystery to Me*. "which left Bob Welch and Christine McVee to take over primary songwriting duties."
